title: Lie Symmetries and Noether Invariants of the Schrödinger Equation with an Oscillating Linear Potential
content: We analyze the point Lie symmetries of the time-dependent Schr\"odinger equation with linear oscillating potential $V(x,t) = \alpha x \cos(\omega t)$, which models the interaction of a charged particle with an electric field in the dipole approximation. The symmetry  algebra is seven-dimensional, with generators $\Xi_1,\ldots,\Xi_7$. Its Levi-Malcev decomposition yields a Levi factor isomorphic to $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})$ and a radical containing a Heisenberg  subalgebra. The quotient by the central generator $\Xi_2$ is isomorphic to the Schr\"odinger algebra $\mathfrak{sch}(1)$ for every $\alpha \neq 0$. The central term $4\alpha^2D^2\Xi_7$ appearing in the commutator $[\Xi_3,\Xi_4]$ is shown to be inessential; it is removed by the redefinition $\Xi_4' = \Xi_4 - 4\alpha^2D^2\Xi_7$, in contrast with the essential central extension of the free Schr\"odinger algebra. The equation is geometrically equivalent to the free Schr\"odinger equation under a time-dependent point transformation combined with a gauge transformation. Noether's theorem yields motion invariants for each generator, including generalizations of the Lewis-Riesenfeld invariants. Reduction of the equation by symmetry produces two families of invariant solutions, namely the Volkov plane wave, which generalizes the particular case $k=0$ obtained previously, and the Airy packet. In phase space, the point-gauge equivalence induces a rigid displacement of the Wigner function.
